concerns.text: Task T006 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it depends on the output of T005 (`data/masked_schema.json`). Running them in parallel could cause a race where T006 reads the file before it is written, violating the producer‑before‑consumer ordering.

Task T007 writes to `data/fallbacks.log`. Subsequent tasks T008 and T009 may also write to the same log (on token‑limit fallback or validation failure). Marking them `[P]` assumes they can run concurrently, but shared‑file writes are not safe without coordination.

Task T008 may append a fallback entry to `data/fallbacks.log` on token‑limit exceedance. This shares the log with T007 and T009, so the `[P]` tag is inaccurate; parallel execution could interleave writes and corrupt the log.
Task T009 also writes to `data/fallbacks.log` on schema validation failure, sharing the same file as T007/T008. The `[P]` tag should be removed or the task should use a thread‑safe logging mechanism.

Task T010 logs successful explanations to `data/success_log.jsonl`. If multiple explanation generations run in parallel, concurrent appends to this file can cause race conditions. The `[P]` tag is therefore unsafe.
